description.narrative: The marine biological diversity of the Kingdom of Tonga is critical to the wellbeing of its people and the foundation of their lifestyle. The Tongan economy heavily relies on the fisheries and marine resources, which in turn depend on the countrys rich biological diversity. However, this rich biological diversity is under threat from multiple sources, including habitat loss, degradation, overexploitation, invasive alien species, pollution, and climate change. Without its wetland and marine biodiversity, Tonga would lose its aesthetic, spiritual, and educational values, which are integral to the peoples wellbeing and traditional way of life.The GEF project is both timely and essential in protecting Tongas indigenous marine species and ecosystems from destructive activities, halting wetland degradation, and restoring degraded mangrove, coral, and seagrass areas. The project aims to control unsustainable resource use and mitigate climate-induced risks through a holistic and integrated Ridge to Reef management approach that builds on the lessons and experiences from the R2R Phase I project. The project will employ an integrated approach consisting of strengthened and effective governance, enhanced capacity for planning and implementing marine resource management strategies built on a solid foundation of a whole-of-community participation, gender equity and social inclusion (GESI) responsive interventions complemented by the development of resilient blue/green livelihoods.

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
